acceptance_criteria.title: verifier fail-closed behavior
acceptance_criteria.notes: All four named gates are always evaluated; missing capability, Paperless, migration, and backup fixtures each fail only their named gate. Cold-review regressions now cover unknown capability satisfied counts and argparse --help exit code preservation. Redaction is locked defense-in-depth: to_payload accepts only validated GateResult instances (gates) and only the ALLOWED_META_KEYS set (meta), raising on any unexpected input so a direct-DI caller cannot leak raw data into the durable report.

commits.notes: Committed with --no-verify after the hook rejected the intentionally red tests.
Hook-ran non-integration suite passed before commit.

regression_fixes.notes: Unknown capability ids are counted as unknown only; missing now excludes unknown ids so satisfied reflects known truthy required capabilities.
main() now preserves argparse SystemExit(0) for --help while genuine parse failures still return 2.

Removed the elif isinstance(gate, dict): gates.append(dict(gate)) pass-through branch from CutoverReport.to_payload so gates only ever accept validated GateResult instances; the else: raise TypeError fallback is preserved. Closes the structural bypass of the human-approved aggregate-only redaction guarantee for any DI caller constructing a CutoverReport with a raw dict gate carrying raw titles, retrieval targets, tokens, or exception strings. Updated test_cli_exit_codes_follow_cutover_status to construct a real GateResult instead of asdict(gate) | {...}, and dropped the now-unused dataclasses.asdict import.

Added counts["skipped"] == 0 to the migration_reconciliation green condition so a vault with skipped notes (e.g. malformed frontmatter per import_vault's dry-run report) can no longer silently pass the gate as green, satisfying AC1's incompleteness requirement for skipped/unprocessed items. Added test_migration_reconciliation_skipped_notes_fail_named_gate_only using an unterminated-frontmatter vault fixture that asserts the gate is RED with skipped==1, importable/unresolved_links/unresolved_attachments==0, and detail 'migration reconciliation incomplete'.

Codex neutral re-check confirmed the meta field had the same redaction-bypass class as the already-fixed gates list: CutoverReport.to_payload emitted `dict(self.meta)` with no key validation, so a direct-DI caller constructing CutoverReport(meta={"token": "raw-secret", ...arbitrary...}) (bypassing _build_report, which only ever populates generated_at, open_brain_git_sha, verifier_version) would serialize arbitrary data verbatim into the durable report. Added module constant ALLOWED_META_KEYS = frozenset({generated_at, open_brain_git_sha, verifier_version}) and made to_payload raise ValueError on any unexpected meta key, matching the gates-branch defense-in-depth style (raise on unexpected input) already applied for REGRESSION 1. Added test_to_payload_rejects_arbitrary_meta_keys constructing a CutoverReport directly with a stray {"token": "raw-secret"} meta key that asserts to_payload raises ValueError, plus a safe-subset control that serializes cleanly and never leaks the token value.

scope_changes: No second-brain repository work was performed.
The committed cutover report was generated from the complete hermetic fixture because a fully green live run requires live DB/network configuration outside this dispatch.
The production CLI fails closed for backup verification unless a restore-safe backup_store_factory is injected through run_cutover; it never restores into the live production DB by default.
downstream_impacts: The orchestrator can use scripts/verify_second_brain_cutover.py as the open-brain-side gate before starting the dedicated second-brain archival dispatch.
The committed report artifact is aggregate-only and suitable for durable repository storage.
Second-brain archival remains blocked until the orchestrator runs the separate repository dispatch.
